messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: inference-prod /v1/chat error rate spike in eu1a — 502s and gRPC stream resets. Alerting on >=5% 5m error rate.
amy: seeing it in dashboards, p50 latency up ~200ms, error rate 12% for that route.
kevin: I can join — looking at NLB & target health first. tagging @mike for oncall handoff.
mike: oncall here. I see NLB unhealthy targets in eu1a, but healthy targets in eu1b. traffic still sticky to eu1a AZ routing.
amy: customers reporting retries, some timeouts. CS notified? @tina-cs
tina-cs: on it, reached out to one impacted customer (early access). They're seeing 502s since ~08:12 UTC. ETA for public notice 20m if high impact.
kevin: running describe-target-health, results: ```json
{"TargetHealthDescriptions":[{"Target":{"Id":"i-0abc","AvailabilityZone":"eu1a"},"TargetHealth":{"State":"unhealthy","Reason":"Unhealthy"}}, {"Target":{"Id":"i-0def","AvailabilityZone":"eu1b"},"TargetHealth":{"State":"healthy"}}]}
```
kevin: also seeing NLB connection queue high on the eu1a proxies (connection backlog > 100k).
alex: quick note — we rolled a new lambda-based auth proxy to eu1a yesterday, it opens long-lived connections to the NLB. Could be related.
mike: plan: 1) drain NLB targets in eu1a for inference-prod route 2) steer traffic to eu1b 3) scale dedicated instances in eu1b if needed. Anyone object?
julia: agreed, do we have cross-AZ capacity headroom? product wants minimal disruption.
amy: eu1b currently at 70% CPU for inference pool, can scale +20% quickly.
kevin: executing step 1: `aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:... --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=10` then `aws elbv2 register-targets --targets Id=i-0def` (already healthy).
ops-bot: Started traffic shift: route inference-prod -> prefer eu1b (policy=zone_fallback).
mike: manually set NLB connection drain on eu1a targets and disabled the lambda-proxy deployment in eu1a: `kubectl -n infra scale deploy auth-proxy --replicas=0 --region=eu1a` (we use region-affinity labels).
kevin: after drain, 502s down to 1.2% and p50 latency settling. gRPC reset counts decreased.
amy: monitoring k/v cache: small KVCACHE miss spike during failover, but fetch rates are normal. Tests show no model degradation.
tina-cs: customers updated: 1 high-touch customer still seeing intermittent errors, sending targeted note.
julia: moving to postmortem/ownership: set oncall mike for now, handoff to infra kevin for deeper root cause.
mike: handoff acknowledged — I'll stay until fully stable and then create incident ticket. next steps: collect NLB kernel metrics, auth-proxy connection behavior, and cloud provider support ticket for possible connection tracking limit in AZ.
kevin: collecting traces and packet counters now; attaching sample pcap snippet (redacted).
amy: thanks team. keeping this thread for updates; if impact drops below 0.5% for 30m we call it mitigated.
incident-bot: Incident status: Mitigated -> Partial (traffic shunted to eu1b) at 08:23 UTC.
mike: follow-ups — revert lambda-proxy to canary, add connection limits and short keepalive, update DNS TTL for quicker failovers, and add NLB connection queue alert for AZ-local saturation.
julia: filing a customer comm for tomorrow and scheduling a postmortem review.
kevin: opening support case with cloud provider referencing possible AZ-level connection throttle during hypervisor maintenance.
amy: last check — error rate stable at 0.4% and latency back to baseline. I'll close once 30m holds.
ops-bot: Logged mitigation actions to incident tracker ID INC-2026-1843.
mike: thanks all — handing to kevin for RCA. :thumbsup:
